# BENQODHI Day 2 Morning - Round Table Participant Guide

*Participant guide for the Day 2 morning round tables, 11 September 2026.*

## Aim and Scope

The Day 2 morning round tables are designed to collect focused expert input for a
possible BENQODHI workshop output such as paper, report, roadmap or policy note.
The central question is how important challenges in health and the life sciences
can become credible, reusable benchmarks for classical, AI-based, hybrid and
quantum algorithms.

The preferred focus is on optimization problems, because optimization is often
presented as one of the main near-term applications of quantum computing. However,
the discussion should not be restricted to optimization if another computational
task is scientifically important and can be stated clearly enough to be assessed.
Inference, sampling, simulation, reconstruction and learning problems can also be
considered when they have a clear health or life-science motivation and a
plausible route to benchmarkability.

The session is not expected to create a complete benchmark repository during the
workshop. The objective is to identify which problems, infrastructure choices,
community mechanisms and policy instruments would make a future benchmark
repository or ecosystem useful beyond the workshop.

The detailed questions and discussion prompts are now kept in each table's own
guide. The shared seed material remains available in the
[seed problem brief](seed-problem-brief.qmd).
